 Around the Mountain West: Perhaps improbably, Wyoming firmly in conference title fight
 New Mexico ranked in AP Top 25 for first time as job speculation continues to swirl around Eck
 UNLV Rebels defensive back Quandarius Keyes (5) reacts after making an interception against the Hawaii Rainbow Warriors during the fourth quarter on Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026, at the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex in Honolulu. Marco Garcia / IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 By 
 Mike McFeely

 What is this? 
 FARGO — The game of the week in the Mountain West Conference is Saturday night in Las Vegas. Wyoming (4-1 league, 5-3 overall) plays at UNLV (3-1, 5-3) in a contest that will have conference title game implications for not only the Cowboys and Rebels, but other teams, too.
 New Mexico leads the Mountain West with a 4-0 record (7-1 overall), and barring a complete collapse in its final four games will likely earn a spot in the league title game. Wyoming is next, followed by UNLV. The Cowboys and Rebels control their title-game destinies. Win out, they are in the championship game.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Mountain West Standings
 Mountain West football standings as of Nov. 5, 2026.
 Conf Overall 
 New Mexico 4-0 7-1 
 Wyoming 4-1 5-3 
 UNLV 3-1 5-3 
 NDSU 4-2 6-2 
 Air Force 3-2 6-2 
 Nevada 2-2 3-5 
 San Jose State 2-3 4-5 
 Hawaii 1-4 2-6 
 UTEP 0-4 1-7 
 N. Illinois 0-4 0-8 
 Three other teams have two conference losses and all have paths to the championship game with some help: NDSU at 4-2, Air Force at 3-2 and Nevada at 2-2.
 The madness begins at 9:30 p.m. Central time on Saturday when Wyoming and UNLV kick off. The game will be carried by CBS Sports Network.
 ““It’s a big week for us and a huge game,” UNLV coach Dan Mullen said to the Vegas media. “Three teams (New Mexico being the third) control where they want to be in November. This is the biggest game so far in the conference this season. Wyoming has an explosive offense and a physical, stout defense. It’s going to be a big challenge for us.”
 The Rebels have been all over the place defensively. They were good in victories over Hawaii and NDSU, but not so good in several other games. That includes last week’s home victory over winless Northern Illinois in which UNLV allowed 493 yards of offense, including 263 after halftime, in a 31-24 victory over a team that is one of the worst offensively in FBS.
 “The urgency players have coming into November, they have to create the urgency and step up and perform on the defensive side of the ball,” Mullen said. “We just didn’t perform well and that’s the disappointing part. You should go into game day with your energy and effort and execution at a high. I know we’ve been banged up but there was an opportunity for guys to go in and make plays.
 “We had over 20 missed tackles and that would have eliminated well over 30 percent of their yards right there. There was a lack of physicality that we don’t usually have. All of those things make for a bad combination.”
 Wyoming, meanwhile, got off to a 2-3 start that included a 28-0 loss in Fargo against the Bison. The Cowboys have won three straight and could finish atop the league and play for the conference championship.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 The Cowboys are also one victory shy of bowl eligibility, which they’ll almost surely reach regardless of Saturday’s outcome. It’d be the first time under third-year head coach Jay Sawvel that Wyoming qualified for a bowl game.
 The folks in Laramie are dubbing this game the biggest of Sawvel’s tenure, which is hard to argue.
 Coming off a bye week, the Cowboys last game was a much-needed and somewhat surprising 28-14 win against Air Force.
 “There’s a lot of people that want to give pats on the back after the Air Force game, but these are the same people that were wanting to shoot arrows at everybody four weeks before it,” Sawvel said to the Wyoming media. “Take the people in the building, and listen to people in the building. Let’s just focus and concentrate on the people in the building.”
 New Mexico head coach Jason Eck. New Mexico Athletics 
 New Mexico ranked
 The first College Football Playoff ranking of 25 teams included only one Group of Six school and it wasn’t New Mexico. That honor went to Boise State of the Pac-12 Conference. But that doesn’t mean the Lobos aren’t getting national recognition.
 New Mexico checked in at No. 22 in this week’s Associated Press Top 25 poll, the first time in program history (nearly 100 years) the Lobos have been ranked.
 New Mexico plays at Nevada on Friday night in Reno.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Unsurprisingly, New Mexico head coach Jason Eck kept things in perspective.
 “Being ranked this week means nothing if you lose this week and get kicked out of the ranking,” Eck said. “So we gotta take care of our business and have great preparation to go play our best football."
 For a program that was down and out for so many years prior to Eck’s arrival in 2025, it’s a big deal to draw attention and perhaps sell more tickets to home games at University Stadium.
 “I think this is a great thing for our fans,” Eck said, “and hopefully it gets them excited about it, gets them thinking about football more. Thinking about, I gotta keep my calendar clear for Saturdays in the fall or Fridays in the fall. Or I gotta keep December open for bowl games and playoffs and things like that. That part of it is great.”
 Speaking of Eck
 Eck continues to be a national media star and continues to be connected to Power Four jobs because of his success at New Mexico.
 Asked by CBS Sports college football reporter Brandon Marcello about his future, Eck did not promise he’d be at New Mexico next year. He cited Nick Saban telling media he wouldn’t leave the Miami Dolphins to coach Alabama, only a short time later to leave the Dolphins to coach Alabama.
 "I never want to do that and lie to people and say something that isn't true," Eck told CBS Sports. "I just know this: I think I have a great job. This community has really rallied behind our team and given us great support, and if I ever leave here, I'm going to be very selective. It's going to have to be an incredible opportunity that I couldn't turn down."
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Mountain West This Week
 Friday, Nov. 6 
 No. 22 New Mexico at Nevada, 8 p.m. (CBS Sports Network)
 Saturday, Nov. 7 
 Northern Illinois at San Jose State, 3 p.m. (MW+)
 Air Force at Army, 6:30 p.m. (CBS)
 Hawaii at UTEP, 8:30 p.m. (FS1)
 Wyoming at UNLV, 9:30 p.m. (CBS Sports Network)
 The Albuquerque Journal reported Eck’s buyout is $4 million through the end of this year, but a clause to cut it to $2 million because the athletic director who hired Eck, Fernando Lovo, left for another job.
 Interestingly, that job happened to be Colorado, where there is speculation that football coach Deion Sanders could leave after this season because of diminishing success. The tie between Lovo and Eck makes for obvious speculation the coach could join the AD in Boulder.
 However, there’s a twist. A separate clause in Eck’s contract, according to the Journal, says the buyout would rise to $4 million if Eck followed Lovo to Colorado.
 Choate knows the score
 If Eck leaves, New Mexico won’t be the only Mountain West school with a football coach opening.
 Northern Illinois is 0-8 and one of the worst teams in FBS, so interim head coach Rob Harley is likely on his way out at season’s end.
 There is much speculation that Scotty Walden will be dismissed at UTEP after the season since the Miners are 1-7 and haven’t shown improvement in Walden’s third season in El Paso. The Miners have one of the worst offenses in FBS and are dead last in average points per game (14.1) among the 138 FBS teams.
 And then there is head coach Jeff Choate at Nevada. The Wolf Pack are far more competitive than Northern Illinois and UTEP, but are 2-2 in the Mountain West and 3-5 overall, in danger of missing a bowl game for the third straight year under Choate and the fifth straight season overall.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Mountain West Odds
 Point spreads for Mountain West Conference football games this week, per BetMGM. As of Nov. 5, 2026.
 No. 22 New Mexico -10 at Nevada
 San Jose State -9.5 vs. Northern Illinois
 Air Force +3 at Army
 Hawaii -9 at UTEP
 UNLV -5.5 vs. Wyoming
 Nevada hosts New Mexico on Friday night and finishes up with Northern Illinois, Hawaii and UNLV. The Wolf Pack need three victories to reach bowl eligibility.
 "I want to go 4-0. Minimum 3-1. And get to a bowl game," Choate said. "That's what this stretch is all about. This is a four-game season one game at a time. You put everything else in the rearview mirror. It's totally irrelevant. What we have in front of us is New Mexico Friday night 6 o'clock at Mackay Stadium. I will be laser focused on that, and then we will go to the next one after that."
 Nevada Sports Net speculated that there is certainly a pathway to six victories, but three defeats in the final four games or again missing a bowl game could also lead to Choate’s firing.
 "I get it, man," Choate said. "Results-based business, and we've got to produce. I think that's in front of us right now. The moment is here. There's a moment right now for us to grab it and say, 'Look, man, Nevada football's back on steady ground. Let's go climb this mountain.'"
